# Plainmaps

The Plainmaps document (kim.quarto.pub/plainmaps) is a fairly long (77 page) PDF. This document provides a lot of examples on how to use some custom functions to create a class of maps using R. These are fairly simple maps (think: country or state borders). Although every attempt was made to simplify the creation of maps, it still takes some effort to learn and follow the instructions.

### An Alternative Approach

It is possible to provide a Large Language Model the document with Plainmaps instructions. Add a few Guidelines (mostly simple instructions in English). Then make a simple request.

*It can be that simple.*

Here is an example using Anthropic's Claude (3.5 Sonnet).

**Prompt**

I have added two files as artifacts. Please use these artifacts to make a map using the Plainmaps style of coding. I need a regional map that shows Nairobi, Mombasa and Kampala.

**Response**

```{r}

## Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(mapdata)
library(plainmaps)
library(sitemaps)

## Initialize defaults for Sitemaps
column <- site_styles()
hide <- site_google_hides()

## Define the theme
plain_background_theme <- theme(
  panel.border = element_blank(),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  panel.background = element_blank(),
  axis.text = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank(),
  axis.title = element_blank()
)

## Define the cities data
cities <- read_csv(col_names = TRUE, file = "
text,lat,lon
Nairobi,-1.2921,36.8219
Mombasa,-4.0435,39.6682
Kampala,0.3476,32.5825
")

## Add the required group column
cities$group <- 1

## Extract the map data for the region
east_africa <- map_data("world", region = c("Kenya", "Uganda", "Tanzania"))

## Create the base map
east_africa_map <- ggplot(data = east_africa, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "darkseagreen3", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +
  plain_background_theme

## Add cities to the map
final_map <- east_africa_map +
  site_points(datatable = cities) +
  site_labels(datatable = cities)

## Display the map
final_map
```

### A Few Observations

The Plainmaps document was written for people to understand. It was not structured for a Large Language Model. It is likely that performance will be improved if the document is organized in a way that is more appropriate for a LLM.

There is likely to be some inconsistency in creating maps this way. As usual, it may take several prompts to get what's needed. You may even need to start afresh.

Claude doesn't always follow all the instructions. Example: there should have been some message suppressing included in the code.
